articles.title: Home Assistant lets AI assistants inspect system logs
articles.dek: An administrator-only connection gives configured AI clients errors and warnings to investigate household system problems.
body: Home Assistant adds an administrator-only connection that lets an AI assistant read recent system errors and warnings. Its first tool searches the system log, giving a configured conversation agent or external AI client evidence for investigating a problem.

Allen Porter separates this system-management connection from Assist’s existing access to exposed household entities. Administrators can filter log entries by severity or source, limit the results and optionally include exception details.

Selecting the connection gives the agent access to those messages and requested traces, which may be sent to its configured AI provider. Its access is not restricted to the entities normally shared with Assist.

pullRequests.title: Add Home Assistant LLM API and system log tool

articles.title: ESPHome speakers can limit playback to paired music servers
articles.dek: Device makers gain pairing codes and a switch for unpaired access, with a Music Assistant compatibility requirement.
body: ESPHome gives Sendspin speakers control over which music servers may play through them. Device makers can offer a fixed pairing code confirmed by a button press, or display a one-time code, and can turn off access for servers that have not paired. Unpaired access remains on by default.

Kevin Ahrendt adds a switch that changes that permission without rebuilding firmware. Turning access off saves the setting immediately, so a power cut cannot undo it. Makers can also configure the switch to default to closed if its saved value is lost.

The encrypted connection requires Music Assistant 2.11.0b4 or newer and the ESP-IDF framework; older Sendspin protocol versions are incompatible. Separate firmware and Python-client support exposes a pairing token through the encrypted Home Assistant connection. That prepares a route for pairing without someone at the speaker, rather than supplying the complete Home Assistant workflow.

articles.title: Music Assistant rejects forged Home Assistant sidebar sign-ins
articles.dek: Identity headers must come through Supervisor, and new account links use a username confirmed by Home Assistant.
body: Music Assistant tightens sign-ins through Home Assistant’s sidebar so another process on the host cannot impersonate a user by sending identity headers to the same address. Those headers are trusted only when the request comes through Supervisor’s proxy.

Marvin Schenkel also requires Home Assistant to confirm the username before matching or creating an account that has not been linked before. Already linked accounts keep their existing sign-in behavior. On a Home Assistant OS test installation, the correction refused a forged request while normal sidebar and integration access still worked.

pullRequests.title: Require the Supervisor as peer for Home Assistant Ingress requests

articles.title: Assist expands Russian commands for music, fans and household lists
articles.dek: Twelve translated intents include media search, mower control and completing list items.
body: Russian speakers gain Assist phrases for more everyday tasks: searching for and playing media, muting and unmuting a player, changing volume relatively, setting fan speed and climate fan mode, and starting or docking a lawn mower. The additions also cover completing and removing list items, completing shopping-list items and spoken responses.

Stanislav Petrashov also corrects absolute volume commands so a request to set a level does not instead increase or decrease it. This is his first contribution to the intents repository, reviewed by HepoH3. These are additions to Home Assistant’s command grammar; they do not establish support in every speech-recognition model.

pullRequests.title: [ru] Add missing sentence translations for 12 intents

articles.title: Home Assistant moves dashboard sections without dragging
articles.dek: Copy, cut and paste carry a whole section between views and dashboards in the same browser tab.
body: Home Assistant adds Copy, Cut, Paste above and Paste below to dashboard section menus. People arranging a long dashboard, particularly on a phone, can move a whole section without dragging it through the page.

The clipboard survives switching views and dashboards in the same tab, and a copied section can be pasted more than once. Cutting removes the original immediately because dashboard edits save automatically; an Undo notice offers a way back.
A completely empty view has no section menu and cannot receive a pasted section yet. This is Xander’s first contribution to Home Assistant’s frontend.

pullRequests.title: Add copy, cut and paste for dashboard sections

articles.title: Matter.js protects a bridge when its connected devices change
articles.dek: Server and client corrections prevent device additions from disrupting Home Assistant and removals from deleting the bridge itself.
body: Matter.js server and its Python client correct failures when devices are added to or removed from a bridge. An addition could reach Home Assistant before the corresponding device information, interrupting its Matter connection. Removing a device made of several parts could instead remove the bridge’s own entry.

Ingo Fischer makes the server send updated device information before announcing an addition and keeps the client’s device relationships intact until the removal arrives. Bridges are also recognized when their grouping point appears somewhere other than the first position.

The changes were checked with a commissioned test bridge and Home Assistant’s actual removal handling. Deeply nested parts that previously appeared on the bridge move to their correct device. Further Home Assistant work is still needed for some bridge relationships and for removing standalone parts.

pullRequests.title: fix: bridge topology resolution, endpoint event order and read consistency

articles.title: Music Assistant preserves high-resolution audio when sources omit its format
articles.dek: Detecting the actual audio prevents an automatic reduction to CD-quality sound.
body: Music Assistant preserves high-resolution audio from sources that do not report its format. Previously, it assumed 44.1 kHz and 16-bit audio before buffering, reducing a recording such as a 24-bit, 48 kHz FLAC to that lower format.

Marcel van der Veldt adds a format check before buffering tracks, audiobooks and podcast episodes. The check gives up after five seconds and leaves playback on its previous path if it cannot identify the format. Radio, live sources and provider-specific streams are unchanged; the correction also prevents WAV and AIFF file headers from playing as noise after seeking.

pullRequests.title: Keep hi-res quality for sources that don't report their audio format

articles.title: Sendspin stops audio buffering from delaying mute and volume changes
articles.dek: The Python server gives control messages priority instead of making listeners wait nearly a minute.
body: Sendspin’s Python server stops holding volume and mute commands behind audio waiting to fill a player’s buffer. With a large buffer, changes could arrive close to a minute late, with several adjustments taking effect together.
Maxim Raznatovski gives those commands priority over audio waiting to be sent. The correction is in the Sendspin library.

pullRequests.title: Fix volume and mute commands delayed behind player audio

articles.title: Home Assistant adjusts Peblar’s custom solar charging
articles.dek: Automations gain the start threshold, grid target and always-charge setting previously kept on the charger.
body: Home Assistant gives Peblar owners control of the settings behind Custom Solar charging. Automations can set how much surplus starts a charging session, the desired power exchange with the grid during charging, and whether charging begins immediately when the car is plugged in.

A zero grid target uses the available surplus; a negative target keeps some power flowing to the grid, while a positive target permits extra grid power. Each control changes only its own setting, preserving the others.
Franck Nijhof builds on the mode selector included in Home Assistant 2026.10. The new controls replace the workaround of sending a raw request to the charger’s internal interface.

pullRequests.title: Set the Peblar Custom Solar thresholds from Home Assistant

articles.title: Home Assistant reads a folding iPhone’s hinge and pose
articles.dek: Three optional sensors report how the phone is folded, while its app is open.
body: Home Assistant’s iPhone app adds optional readings for a folding phone’s hinge angle, hinge status and pose. Automations can distinguish a closed or fully open phone and use the angle between its halves.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves derives the pose from the hinge and device orientation, with states including book, laptop and flat face down. Ambiguous positions remain partially open rather than guessing a pose.
The sensors depend on the hinge interfaces introduced in iOS 27.1 and update only while the app is on screen. They are opt-in and disappear on devices that report no hinge.

articles.title: ESPHome prepares seven more chip types with ready-made firmware
articles.dek: The browser installer adds starter images and a serial route for changing Wi-Fi settings.
body: ESPHome Web adds ready-made starter firmware for seven Beken, Lightning and Realtek chip types. Makers can prepare these boards for use without first compiling a device-specific file; the browser installer keeps an option for their own firmware too.

J. Nick Koston adds images for BK7231N, BK7231T, BK7238, BK7252, LN882H, RTL8710B and RTL8720C. A new Configure Wi-Fi action uses the serial connection to change network settings on firmware with Improv serial support, alongside the existing fallback access-point route.

The starter images were installed and connected on BK7238 and RTL8720C hardware; the other listed images passed builds. Serial Wi-Fi setup was verified on RTL8720C. Beken and Lightning boards use their logging serial port for Wi-Fi setup, which can differ from the installation connection.

articles.title: Music Assistant limits what device artwork links can open
articles.dek: Artwork extraction accepts local files or web URLs, and helper processes stop inheriting Home Assistant tokens.
body: Music Assistant restricts artwork references reported by network devices before passing them to its media tools. Previously, a device could supply an address for another supported streaming protocol and make the cover-art loader contact it.

Marvin Schenkel limits extraction to existing local files or ordinary web URLs and prevents one kind of input from opening the other through an embedded reference. Helper processes also stop inheriting Home Assistant’s Supervisor tokens. Ordinary web cover extraction continues to work.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s installer prepares private reports when setup fails
articles.dek: Recovery controls distinguish safe retries, while problem reports leave out credentials and server details.
body: Home Assistant’s installer gives failed installations clearer recovery steps and a manual way to prepare a problem report. Error screens distinguish a safe retry from cases where a virtual machine may already exist and needs attention outside the installer.

About and error screens offer a diagnostic preview, a copy control and access to local logs. Reports include the installer version, operating system, installation stage and recent safe log records, while leaving out credentials, server details and user paths. Reporting remains manual, with no telemetry enabled.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s Android app limits where it sends credentials
articles.dek: An encrypted address must also belong to a known server before it can receive login details.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app checks that an HTTPS address is a known server before sending it credentials. The existing check accepted every HTTPS address, treating encryption alone as sufficient.
Timothy adds the known-address requirement, with review by Joris Pelgröm.

articles.title: Home Assistant tests automation steps while they stay disabled
articles.dek: Run action and Test execute the selected step without enabling it for normal runs.
body: Home Assistant lets people try a disabled action or condition on its own while building or troubleshooting an automation. Previously, Run action and Test reported success but did nothing for disabled steps.

Marcin Bauer makes those individual controls execute the selected step. Ordinary automation and script runs still skip disabled steps, so testing one does not require enabling it in the live sequence.

articles.title: ESPHome reads touch on Waveshare’s 1.46-inch round display
articles.dek: The SPD2010 controller joins the built-in touchscreen options.
body: ESPHome adds the touch controller used by the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.46, giving makers a built-in way to read touches on its round screen. It supports either an interrupt signal or regular polling, with the board’s 412-by-412 calibration as its default.

Guillaume Rischard supplies the controller support and configuration guide. The implementation was validated on hardware; it adds touch input rather than establishing complete support for every part of the display board.

articles.title: Music Assistant shows Apple Music names in the chosen language
articles.dek: Catalog and library requests use a supported language instead of the storefront’s default.
body: Music Assistant asks Apple Music for names in the user’s language when that storefront supports it. An English setup connected to the Japanese storefront can therefore receive “Taylor Swift” instead of her name in Katakana.

Marvin Schenkel applies the choice to catalog and library requests, preferring an exact locale and then the same language in another locale. Names already synchronized change after a resync; unsupported languages retain the storefront’s default.
